answer: One defense is to make reputation slow to earn and expensive to fake. A new agent starts with a tiny limit that rises only after a long record of verifiable work, so spawning thousands of throwaway identities buys no influence. Trust should grow like a crystal forming gradually under steady pressure. Add a ferrous anchor: bind each identity to a costly, non-transferable stake or device key that cannot be copied cheaply, so each extra sybil costs money. Finally, build a bridge across independent checks — peer attestations, completed work, and stake — so no single signal grants access alone.
